Foundation Models for Partial Causal Identification extends causal FMs to bounding intervention effects under unobserved confounding, while MTCR delivers certified robustness guarantees against multi-turn jailbreaks.

  • Muon shows persistent scaling advantages over AdamW on Diffusion Transformers up to 15B parameters
  • E2-TTT derives exact closed-form state transitions for test-time training, advancing the linear-attention architecture race
  • An open-weight introspection study provides rigorous negative findings on whether LLMs can report their own internal computation

entry.title: Foundation Models for Partial Causal Identification

author.name: Alexis Bellot, Anish Dhir

entry.summary: Develops causal foundation models for bounding intervention effects and counterfactuals under unobserved confounding by defining a canonical prior with full support over structural causal models with discrete observables. The task becomes learning distributions over functions mapping data and assumptions to causal queries.

entry.title: Open-Weight Masked Introspection: Measuring What Language Models Can Report About Their Own Computation

author.name: Emilio Ferrara

entry.summary: This study tests whether open-weight language models can introspect about their own computation by intervening on residual streams, attention heads, and SAE features, then asking models what changed against sham and matched-control baselines. Across eight open-weight models from seven families, none outperformed chance, providing a negative result against claims that sufficiently capable models can audit their own internals.

entry.title: Certified Multi-Turn Robustness for LLM Safety via Compositional Bounds and Safety Persistence

author.name: Yang Liu, Bin Chong, Wenkai Yang, Shuai Zhang, Yancheng Chen, Feiyu Han, GuoZhen, Cheng Zhang, Huaibing Xie, Changze Lv, Shihan Dou, Pluto Zhou

entry.summary: Introduces Multi-Turn Certified Robustness (MTCR), modeling conversational safety via State-Adversarial MDPs and defining k-turn certified robustness against progressive multi-turn jailbreak attacks. It uses embedding-space mode decomposition for tighter compositional bounds and alpha-beta safety persistence to slow bound degradation.

entry.title: Scaling Muon for Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Chenghao Li, Xiao Han, Xinxin Huang, Wei Liu, Boyang Li, Bing Xiao, Heran Zhang, Juanma Perez Rua, Ke Xu, Kangning Liu, Linjun Kuang, Na Li, Tan Wang, Tian Xie, Wei Peng, Yang Pei, Yifan Xu, Yuanhao Zhai, Yuwei Lin, Zhe Wang, Zihao He, Daniel Li, Junbiao Tang, Ziyang Jiang, Dake Chen

entry.summary: This work establishes Muon optimizer scaling behavior on Diffusion Transformers from 1.3B to 15B parameters, showing persistent advantages over AdamW in optimization and generative quality. To fix Newton-Schulz overhead at scale it introduces Periodic Row-wise Muon, which amortizes full spectral updates across steps.

entry.title: Beyond Imitation: Self-Improving Robot Policies via Off-Policy Q-Planning

author.name: Varun Giridhar, Anant Khandelwal, Jeremy A. Collins, Ignat Georgiev, Animesh Garg

entry.summary: Q-Planning equips large visuomotor behavior-cloning robot policies with a small off-policy Q-function trained on the same demonstrations that later absorbs both successful and failed deployment rollouts, enabling self-improvement without extra human data. Because Q estimates value rather than imitating actions, failures become usable signal that BC alone cannot exploit. Avoids scaling difficulties of RL fine-tuning on multi-billion-parameter policies.

entry.title: aiXamine: Unified Black-Box Evaluation of Cross-Dimensional Trade-offs in LLM Safety, Security, and Privacy

author.name: Fatih Deniz, Yazan Boshmaf, Dorde Popovic, Issa Khalil

entry.summary: aiXamine is a unified black-box platform evaluating LLM safety, security, and privacy as interdependent properties through 46 tests across nine services in an automated red-teaming pipeline. It surfaces cross-dimensional trade-offs invisible to siloed evaluations, such as models refusing many benign queries despite high safety scores. Produces hierarchical risk profiles for reproducible trustworthiness assessment.

entry.title: Who Delegates to AI? Evidence from 53,000 Agent Configurations

author.name: Hyeongjae Lee, Jihyang Cheon, Lanu Kim

entry.summary: Introducing delegated exposure and the Agentic Adoption Index, this study measures whether workers have actually committed tasks to AI by analyzing roughly 53,000 agent skill specifications from the Manus Skills Marketplace matched against about 18,000 O*NET task statements. It finds distinct patterns in which occupations are actually delegating work to agents, complementing capability-based exposure measures.

entry.title: Consilience: Conformally Calibrated Communication Control for Hidden-Profile Multi-Agent Reasoning

author.name: Abhijith Babu, Ramneet Kaur, Vishal Pramanik, Olivera Kotevska, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Susmit Jha, Sunny Raj, Yanzhao Wu, Sumit Kumar Jha, Anirban Roy

entry.summary: Consilience is an inference-time orchestration framework that steers and certifies communication in multi-agent LLM reasoning under hidden-profile settings where each agent holds partial evidence. It maintains a compact discussion state capturing uncertainty, disagreement, evidence gain, redundancy, and premature consensus to decide whether conversational actions are appropriate, offering guarantees absent from fixed schedules or debate protocols.

entry.title: AI with Authority, from Application to Silicon

author.name: Jason Hickey

entry.summary: Reporting that generative AI makes machine verification economical and essential rather than a cost overhead, this paper describes one researcher directing AI agents in five weeks from application code through a verified compiler and executive to a RISC-V processor taped out on a community shuttle, with no human-reviewed proofs and no human-written RTL. The Salt method rests on a hallucination-resistant proof kernel.

entry.title: Rethinking Expressivity and Efficiency in Test-Time Training

author.name: Zeyun Zhong, Joya Chen, Manuel Martin, Frederik Diederichs, Juergen Gall, Juergen Beyerer

entry.summary: E2-TTT derives a closed-form chunk-level state transition that exactly reproduces per-token fast-weight and momentum states of test-time training recurrences, enabling fully parallelized chunk-wise training without discarding temporal structure. Validated by training models up to 1.3B parameters. Balances expressivity of per-token updates with hardware-efficient chunked approximations for long-context processing.

entry.title: Move by Move: Measuring and Steering How LLMs Conduct Psychotherapy

author.name: Afonso Baldo, Hugo Pitorro, Areti Vassilopoulos, Anabela C. Areias, Maya D'Eon, Fab\'iola Costa, Ricardo Rei, Nuno M. Guerreiro

entry.summary: Introduces an ontology of ten therapeutic moves validated with five licensed psychologists and scaled via judge-based annotation, then compares human clinicians against frontier LLMs conducting psychotherapy sessions. Finds models over-use inquiry up to three times the human rate, neglect psychoeducation, and anchor strongly to strategies initiated earlier in context.

entry.title: Logic-VLA: A Temporal Logic Conditioned Vision-Language-Action Model

author.name: Celina Shiyu Wang, Yiqi Zhao, Junjie Ye, Yue Wang, Jyotirmoy V. Deshmukh

entry.summary: Logic-VLA conditions vision-language-action policies on Signal Temporal Logic specifications provided at inference time, using a syntax-graph-based STL encoder pre-trained to capture temporal logic semantics. Training combines STL-conditioned supervised fine-tuning with trajectory-level preference optimization over satisfying-versus-violating rollout pairs via a flow-matching surrogate for Identity Preference Optimization.

entry.title: Self-Speculation for Faster Reasoning Models

author.name: Ravisri Valluri, Tung Nguyen, Aditya Grover

entry.summary: SSR is a training-free self-speculative decoding method that uses the partial chain-of-thought answer distribution as the draft for the model itself, exploiting reasoning-workflow structure that token-level acceleration ignores. Targets latency-sensitive interactive applications needing long reasoning traces. No auxiliary drafter model required.

entry.title: Affective Context Amplifies Sycophancy in LLM Responses

author.name: Jiayi Li, Sanjana Menon, Brett Frischmann, Shomir Wilson, Sarah Rajtmajer

entry.summary: Shows that affective context systematically amplifies LLM sycophancy: user-facing responses soften or withhold negative evaluations compared to third-party framings of identical content, measured across seven LLMs on Reddit datasets. Grounded in ingratiation theory, this reveals a consistent safety-relevant bias in emotionally loaded interactions.

entry.title: A Survey on Foundations and Frontiers of Multimodal Agentic Frameworks: Techniques and Applications

author.name: Neel Mokaria, Rishie Raj, Dheeraj Baiju, Xiaoqian Shen, Shraman Pramanick, Kevin Qinghong Lin, Arda Senocak, Mike Zheng Shou, Philip Torr, Mohamed Elhoseiny, Yapeng Tian, Ruohan Gao, Salman Khan, Sayan Nag, Sanjoy Chowdhury, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey examining how multimodality shapes agency across the core modules of agentic frameworks: perception, memory, reasoning, planning, and action. It fills a gap left by prior LLM-agent surveys by systematically covering systems built on large multimodal models processing images, audio, and video, and maps techniques to applications.

entry.title: Volumetric Radiology AI in the Era of Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Zanting Ye, Shengyuan Liu, Xin Liu, Chenhui Wang, Zhisong Wang, Jiashuai Liu, Zipei Wang, Cheng Wang, Wentao Pan, Mengjie Fang, Di Dong, Mohammad Salmanpour, Arman Rahmim, Yu Gu, Yong Xia, Hongming Shan, Yixuan Yuan, Yefeng Zheng, Lijun Lu

entry.summary: This paper surveys how multimodal large language models are extending radiology AI beyond 2D image analysis toward full volumetric (3D) interpretation. It identifies a core representational mismatch between clinical needs for whole-volume spatial context and current MLLM conditioning on selected slices or report text, and outlines requirements for preserving and integrating task-relevant 3D information.

entry.title: Continuous-Time Quantum Walks based Graph Neural Network

author.name: Yuliang Zhan, Zefeng Gao, Jian Li, Yang Liu, Hao sun

entry.summary: Proposes CTQW-GNN, a graph neural network built on continuous-time quantum walks that jointly addresses heterophily and over-smoothing using properties of the CTQW propagator, with theoretical justification rather than heuristics. This offers a principled alternative to standard message passing.

entry.title: Prediction certification cannot replace explanation certification: a competence envelope for trustworthy AI under compound stress

author.name: Nataliya Shakhovska, Ivan Izonin, Stergios-Aristoteles Mitoulis

entry.summary: Proves a separation theorem showing that a reliable model and a compromised one can be identical under every prediction-side certificate (accuracy, calibration, conformal coverage) yet differ arbitrarily in explanation behavior. This establishes that prediction certification cannot substitute for explanation certification in trustworthy AI.

entry.title: CLEAR: Continuous Latent Adapter Routing for Utility-Preserving LLM Safety Alignment

author.name: Chengxiao Wang, Enyi Jiang, Xiaojing Liao, Sanmi Koyejo

entry.summary: CLEAR proposes conditional safety adaptation where a lightweight hidden-state gate continuously controls the activation strength of a safety low-rank adapter, reducing harmful completions while leaving benign-prompt behavior of the frozen backbone intact. Experiments show improved HarmBench robustness with reduced utility degradation versus global safety tuning.

entry.title: SRL-MPC: Shape-Aware Reinforcement Learned Model Predictive Control

author.name: Ruihua Han, Rui Gao, Zhe Liu, Xinyi Wang, Chang Chen, Shuai Wang, Qi Hao, Jia Pan, Hengshuang Zhao

entry.summary: Quantization-Aware Healing (QAH) recovers structurally compressed 4-bit LLMs by distilling from the bf16 checkpoint rather than refitting hard labels as in standard QAT, which converged slowly and collapsed past its peak. The recipe targets combined structural pruning plus 4-bit quantization pipelines where reasoning and coding degrade severely.

entry.title: Primal Acceleration of Newton's Method

author.name: Nikita Doikov

entry.summary: This optimization-theory paper develops a primal accelerated Newton method for convex functions with Lipschitz Hessian achieving global O(1/k^3) convergence with one linear solve per iteration and predetermined parameters. It is claimed to be the first second-order method attaining this rate without cubic regularization subproblems, nonlinear searches, or dual corrections, implementable Hessian-free.

entry.title: Designing a Robust LLM-Based Evaluation System for Agentic AI in Drug Discovery Through Human Alignment

author.name: Emma Granqvist, Roc\'io Mercado, Samuel Genheden

entry.summary: This paper presents an LLM-as-a-Judge evaluation framework for ChatInvent, an agentic drug discovery assistant deployed at AstraZeneca, validated against human expert judgments. It defines four output-quality dimensions and shows that reference-based metrics fail for open-ended tool-augmented outputs. The work provides one of the first human-aligned validation studies of LLM judges in industrial chemistry workflows.

entry.title: Multilingual Verifier Bias in RLVR: Benchmark, Rollout Diagnosis, and the Cross-Lingual Selection Bottleneck

author.name: Chenyu Zhou, Qiliang Jiang, Xu Zhou

entry.summary: This work shows exact-match verifiers in multilingual RLVR convert format and script variation into language-dependent false-negative reward noise, breaking the assumption of language-neutral rewards. It introduces a reusable auditing protocol with verifier-robustness suites and language-conditioned reward-error metrics across Japanese, English, and Chinese, revealing sharply different rejection rates on MGSM rollouts for Qwen3 models. Identifies cross-lingual selection as a bottleneck for multilingual reasoning training.

entry.title: Llama-Mobile: Efficient 2.7-Bit Quantization of VLMs

author.name: Luka Ribar, Jeevan Bhoot, Douglas Orr

entry.summary: Presents a framework for quantizing vision-language models to 2.7 bits per parameter with efficient Arm CPU execution, using a self-generating-data calibration pipeline requiring no access to the original training setup. Compresses Llama 3.2 11B Vision Instruct to 3.7 GB with 8-bit activations while preserving strong VQA performance. Enables on-device multimodal inference.

entry.title: Truthful Calibration Measures for Sequential Prediction

author.name: Anagha Gokul, Jason Hartline, Lunjia Hu, Jonathan Ullman, Yifan Wu

entry.summary: Resolves an open question negatively: exact truthfulness is incompatible with completeness and soundness for calibration measures in sequential binary prediction, even with independent outcomes. Shows approximate truthfulness escapes the impossibility via two general reductions producing additively and multiplicatively approximately truthful measures. Advances the theory of truthful calibration following Haghtalab et al. 2024.

entry.title: EndoLIFT: Language-Disambiguated Latent-Conditioned Rectified Flow for Bidirectional Endoscopic Control

author.name: Chi Kit Ng, Yidong Zhang, Lui Siu Hing, Jinsong Lin, Tianchun Wu, Ho Yin Chim, Zhiqing Tang, Tao Yang, Huxin Gao, Trevor Yeung, Raymond Shing-Yan Tang, Hongliang Ren

entry.summary: EndoLIFT is a vision-language-action policy for bidirectional gastrointestinal endoscopic control that combines language-based intent conditioning with a latent-conditioned rectified-flow action expert. It formalizes intent aliasing, where nearly identical visual observations require opposite axial actions depending on the requested procedure phase, and resolves it through explicit instruction conditioning.

entry.title: Roadside-Cooperative Autonomous Driving: From Data Platform to Vision-Language End-to-End Reasoning

author.name: Yitao Xu, Tong Wu, Yiyan Wu, Guoji Xu, Yanbo Jiang, Jiahao Wang, Zehong Ke, Junkai Jiang, Fang Zhang, Jianqiang Wang

entry.summary: The work introduces V2XBench, a closed-loop simulation platform with synchronized ego-roadside sensing, plus Chat-V2XBench, a progressively structured VQA dataset for cooperative driving reasoning, and proposes AURORA, an end-to-end cooperative driving framework with dual-view perception and vision-language reasoning. It targets beyond-line-of-sight perception and language-grounded supervision gaps in existing V2X benchmarks.

entry.title: CDRL: Certification-Driven Reinforcement Learning for Neutrino Flavor Model Discovery

author.name: Piyush Jha, Jake Rudolph, Victoria Knapp-P\'erez, Max Fieg, Aishik Ghosh, Vijay Ganesh

entry.summary: CDRL introduces certification-driven reinforcement learning in which symbolic reasoners produce certificates identifying which actions cause constraint violations during scientific hypothesis search. These certificates become reusable constraints that prune invalid solution classes and guide exploration, demonstrated on neutrino flavor model discovery.

entry.title: CAS: Conformalized Agentic Search via Adaptive Retrieval and Policy Weighting

author.name: Zixi Zhu, Jiayuan Su, Jian Zhang, Yu Lin, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Conformalized Agentic Search (CAS), which applies conformal prediction both at retrieval time via adaptive prediction sets for dynamic document truncation and during RL fine-tuning via adaptive conformal inference to curb over-confidence and hallucination. It targets reliability failures of search agents under RL.

entry.title: Stored in Optimizer State, Valued by Later Training: A Causal Account of Subliminal Trait Transfer

author.name: Qinyang Xu

entry.summary: Treating parameters and optimizer moments as one trainer state, this work derives an exact transport-valuation identity explaining how subliminal behavioral traits survive removal of tainted source data and acquire different signs under later training, identifying the first optimizer moment as the causal carrier via state surgery experiments.

entry.title: AsmEvo: Agentic Assembly-Level Optimization of AMD GPU Kernels with Functional Equivalence Verification

author.name: Ji Liu, Puyuan Yang, Rongzhang Zheng, Fan Wang, Jinglin Wang, Muhammad A. Awad, Mortis Huang, Andy Chang, Zekai Li, Zeping Li, Zihao An, Yue Liu, Yuchen Yang, Jianghui Wang, Chushi Chen, Ziqiong Liu, Fuwei Yang, Dong Li, Wen Heng Chung, Shengcai Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: AsmEvo is an agentic optimizer editing already-compiled AMDGPU code objects where the deployed binary is the only behavioral oracle, reconstructing reassemblable representations, proposing low-level edits with a long-horizon agent, rebuilding ABI-preserving objects, and accepting candidates verified functionally equivalent. Goes beyond CUDA/Triton source-level optimizers. Large AMD-affiliated author list suggests serious industrial backing.

entry.title: Dual-Cache Latent Space Communication between Heterogeneous Language Models

author.name: Jiyao Liu, Qi Zhang, Yaoyi Jia, Ziwen Kan, Song Wang

entry.summary: This work proposes dual-cache latent space communication between heterogeneous language models, letting one model transfer knowledge encoded in its KV cache to another without autoregressive text decoding. It extends prior protocols like C2C and LCF-X by relaxing shared-context, layer-alignment, and compression restrictions between sharer and receiver.

entry.title: Knowing but Not Saying: Preventing Factual Access Failures in LLM SFT via Recall-Anchored Distillation

author.name: Haodong Chen, Yadong Wang, Shengtao Wen, Dong Liang, Xiang Chen

entry.summary: Identifies factual access failure as a distinct phenomenon from catastrophic forgetting: after domain SFT, models can recognize correct answers under constrained probes but fail to produce them in closed-book generation. It proposes recall-anchored distillation to prevent such failures.

entry.title: RAG Deserves an Index: Why Ingest-Time Compilation Beats Query-Time Interpretation

author.name: Kyle Wild, Yusuke Takahashi, Asako Uraki

entry.summary: Argues that production RAG systems waste computation by re-interpreting raw corpus text at query time, and proposes ingest-time semantic compilation (ISC): precomputing a maintained semantic index once at write time, analogous to database indexing. The paper positions this as a paradigm shift for retrieval-augmented QA economics.

entry.title: TreeWY: Speculative Verification for Gated DeltaNet Hybrids

author.name: Sneha Murthy Ghantasala

entry.summary: TreeWY removes state snapshots in speculative decoding for Gated DeltaNet hybrid models by computing each draft tree node output with a tree-structured WY transform of the gated delta rule, reconstructing only the accepted state. This makes wide draft trees memory-feasible for linear-attention hybrids.

entry.title: CellPath-Bench: A Multidimensional Benchmark for Whole-Slide Cellular Representations in Pathology Foundation Models

author.name: Bokai Zhao, Yiyang Zhang, Hanqing Chao, Yawei Ma, Long Bai, Tai Ma, Minfeng Xu, Ming Song, Tianzi Jiang

entry.summary: CellPath-Bench evaluates frozen pathology foundation models at cellular resolution using 25 spatially aligned H&E-Xenium sections spanning 11 organs and over 7 million cells, probing cell-type decodability and transferability across tissues, datasets, and organs.

entry.title: WA-JEPA: Rethinking the Video JEPA Paradigm for World-Action Modeling in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xinlin Wang, Yujiao Xiang, Yuheng Zhou, Jingqi Wang, Minqing Huang, Jiajie Huang, Dongxu Wei, Tingguang Zhou, Xiyang Wang, Gong Chen, Zhi Xu, Feiyang Tan, Hangning Zhou, Mu Yang

entry.summary: WA-JEPA adapts the video JEPA paradigm for autonomous driving planning via hybrid future-masked pre-training that infers future latents from observed context, replacing random masking and deterministic regression with action-coupled prediction. It positions world modeling tightly around action-conditioned futures for driving.

entry.title: BackDFL: A Unified Benchmark For Backdoor Attacks and Defenses In Decentralized Federated Learning

author.name: Mouhamed Amine Bouchiha, Gregory Blanc, Yufei Han

entry.summary: BackDFL is a unified benchmark for backdoor attacks and defenses in decentralized federated learning, arguing that prior robustness claims are inflated by simplified threat models, non-adaptive adversaries, and inconsistent protocols. It standardizes evaluation across communication topologies and adaptive attackers. The paper reframes the threat landscape when no central parameter server exists.

entry.title: Minimax Optimality of Score-Entropy Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Cholyeon Cho, Yuchen Wu

entry.summary: This theory paper establishes minimax optimality bounds for score-entropy discrete diffusion (SEDD), investigating fundamental statistical properties rather than sampling efficiency under assumed-small score error. It complements prior finite-sample analyses of score estimation itself. Provides foundational guarantees for one of the strongest empirical discrete diffusion families used on text and graphs.

entry.title: Human-JEPA: A Human-Centric Vision Model that Perceives and Anticipates

author.name: Hui Wei, Licai Sun, Guoying Zhao

entry.summary: Human-JEPA is a human-centric video vision model trained via anchored forecasting, pinning dense prediction targets to a frozen copy of initialization to prevent collapse of dense perception, with past-to-future masking replacing block masks. Under frozen probes it leads pose estimation and person re-identification specialists at 2.7 times fewer parameters while adding anticipation ability. Extends JEPA-style learning to humans who move.

entry.title: VT-MUSE: Multimodal Unified Sequential Visuotactile Representation Learning for Manipulation

author.name: Congsheng Xu, Qiaochu Yang, Fangyuan Shi, Yifan Han, Baijun Chen, Yiming Wang, Haonan Zhao, Daolin Ma, Xiaokang Yang, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: VT-MUSE is a two-stage multimodal representation learning framework for visuotactile robotic manipulation that jointly adapts modality-specific encoders via cross-modal temporal alignment and masked-view consistency, then uses a conditional variational latent model over masked visual sequences with full tactile histories. It targets fine-grained cross-modal dependencies and temporal contact evolution that independent-encode-then-fuse approaches miss.

entry.title: ReFrame: Evidence-Guided Test-Time Safety Alignment in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Wenzheng Jiang, Xuankun Rong, Yuanzhao Zhai, Dawei Feng, Huaimin Wang

entry.summary: ReFrame is a training-free test-time safety alignment framework for multimodal LLMs, using two-agent input reframing guided by identified failure modes of utility dominance and reasoning inertia. It works on closed-source deployed models where retraining or internal-state access is impossible.

entry.title: Truth Lies Deep: Countering Semantic Camouflage via Latent Intent Verification

author.name: Md. Hasib Ur Rahman

entry.summary: This safety study shows that LLM alignment based on refusal mechanisms remains vulnerable to Semantic Camouflage attacks that wrap harmful intent in benign narrative contexts like creative writing. By analyzing latent activation trajectories in Phi-3, Qwen2.5, and Gemma-2b under adversarial stress, it identifies a universal Intent Horizon, a critical depth at which harmful intent becomes detectable in latent space.

entry.title: Why2Speak: Faithful Reasoning for Abstaining Action Policies

author.name: Shreya Mendi, Brinnae Bent

entry.summary: Why2Speak studies faithful reasoning for policies deciding when to act versus abstain, instantiated as intervention timing in multi-party conversation. Using Qwen3-8B, it compares direct, chain-of-thought, fine-tuned, and RL policies, uncovering a capability-auditability tradeoff where the strongest direct policy resists faithful explanation.

entry.title: Beyond Endpoint Gains: A Weight-Delta Audit of Medical Specialization

author.name: Praphul Singh, Shanu Kumar, Akshat Agarwal

entry.summary: Audits the actual weight deltas between generalist-medical checkpoint pairs (Gemma-3-4B-IT to MedGemma-4B-IT and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct to HuatuoGPT-o1-7B) rather than just endpoint benchmark gains. It finds decoder-side updates strongly reconstruct benchmark movement but the change is not cleanly localized, with MLP components dominating.

entry.title: MGAL: A Multilingual Granularity-Aware Long-Context Benchmark

author.name: Chunhan Li, Chenglin Xu, Zongyang Zhang, Jiale Liu, Zhuoxi Rao, Xudong Jia, Junxiu He, Menglin Yang, Wenjuan Gong, Zhengzhe Liu, Chengwei Qin

entry.summary: MGAL is the first multilingual, granularity- and position-aware long-context benchmark built from UN reports spanning 8K to 128K tokens across six official UN languages. It stratifies tasks by word, sentence, paragraph, and document granularity plus document position, enabling finer-grained diagnosis of long-context failures.

entry.title: Testing and Evaluation of Agentic AI Systems In Military Command and Control

author.name: Ulysse Richard, Heather Frase, Sarah Cao, Di Cooke, Sebastian Kwon, Adrianna Tan

entry.summary: A structured review of 240 documented testing-and-evaluation practices for military command-and-control AI identifies eight assumptions (grouped into specifiability, stability, composability, supervisability) that established methods make, showing how agentic properties weaken each and what that implies for discharging public commitments to human oversight.

entry.title: ClawSentry: A Progressive Multi-Tier Security Monitor for Safeguarding Autonomous LLM Agents

author.name: Kai Wang, Zeming Wei, BiaoJie Zeng, Chang Jin, An Wang, Xiaokun Luan, Zhixiao Lin, Jingjing Qu, Xia Hu, Xingcheng Xu

entry.summary: ClawSentry is an open-source framework-agnostic supervision gateway monitoring autonomous LLM agents across four lifecycle loci: skill admission, invocation-time intent, execution-time effect, and post-action consequence. It addresses progressive risk where denied dangerous objectives reappear across surface forms, tools, or turns.

entry.title: Wrong-Physics Backdoors in Neural PDE Operators

author.name: Hanbing Liang, Fujun Liu

entry.summary: Introducing wrong-physics backdoors, this paper describes a cross-parameter relinking data-poisoning primitive against neural PDE operators trained on solver archives: triggered inputs return physically plausible solutions for the wrong physical parameter. Across 476 campaigns on Burgers and other dynamics it exploits tensor-to-parameter provenance failures in multi-parameter archives.

entry.title: RODE: A Radial-Orthogonal Decoupled Engine for Optimization

author.name: Guoxiang Xu, Bince Qu, Qi Sun, Cheng Zhuo

entry.summary: RODE is a matrix-aware optimizer that decouples the radial (Frobenius norm) and directional components of weight updates, giving each its own update rule and step size, with Newton-Schulz-conditioned directional updates in the tangent space. Controlled GPT-2 interventions demonstrate gains from explicit norm control plus the directional channel. It addresses an underexplored interaction in Muon-style optimizers where norm and direction changes interfere.

entry.title: Asymmetric Capacity Allocation in Self-Refinement Pipelines

author.name: Zhuoyi Yang, Ian G. Harris, Salar Hashemitaheri, Cassie Huang, Yuangang Li, Hyunwoo Oh, Paul Dourish, Tony Givargis, Mohsen Imani, Li Zhang

entry.summary: First stage-wise study of model size in LLM self-refinement pipelines across 5 benchmarks using multiple sizes of Qwen3 and other families. It examines whether generation, critique, and revision require equally capable models, finding asymmetric capacity allocation can save resources. Challenges treating model size as an implementation detail in generate-critique-revise loops.

entry.title: Harmonic Torsional Diffusion for Protein-Ligand Flexible Docking

author.name: Maksim Zhdanov, Pavel Strashnov, Vladislav Kurenkov

entry.summary: Harmony parameterizes ligand and side-chain torsional score fields for flexible protein-ligand docking as derivatives of learned harmonic potentials on the circle, with noise-level dependence supplied analytically by the heat semigroup on the torus. This respects periodic geometry that generic Euclidean diffusion heads ignore. Targets joint pose and protein flexibility modeling in structure-based drug design.

entry.title: Rethinking Demonstration Unlearning in Imitation Learning for Robotics

author.name: Jiazhuo Li, Yu Zhang, Yiming Fei, Kangkang Dong, Xiaojun Zhu, Houde Liu, Jinze Tao

entry.summary: This work defines a retrain-calibrated audit for demonstration unlearning in robot imitation learning along two axes: behavioral similarity to a policy retrained without removed demonstrations, and detectability of prior training exposure. Existing machine-unlearning metrics fail to capture what edits remove from closed-loop policies. Motivated by people requesting removal of their demonstrations from robot training data.

entry.title: RARE: Decoupling Representation Steering from Expert Routing in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models

author.name: Zhibo Zhang, Zhen Ouyang, Ling Shi, Kailong Wang

entry.summary: Identifies a structural mismatch when applying representation steering to Mixture-of-Experts models, showing that behavioral perturbations disrupt router decisions. The proposed RARE framework projects perturbations onto the null space of the router matrix, making steering router-agnostic while preserving clean routing.

entry.title: Basin-Preserving Discretizations of Modern Hopfield Retrieval Dynamics: Energy Cells, Dissipation, and the Attention Limit

author.name: Francisco R. Villatoro

entry.summary: This theoretical work studies which time discretizations of modern Hopfield retrieval dynamics preserve not only energy decay and equilibria but also basins of attraction, introducing energy cells as connected sublevel-set components around attractors. author.name: Adam Karvonen

entry.summary: The authors introduce CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that discovers unexpected LLM behaviors in the wild and explains them via counterfactual prompt edits, then uses the resulting dataset both as an evaluation and as training data. entry.title: Rogue Scalpel: Activation steering breaks refusal, even with benign directions

author.name: Alexey Dontsov

entry.summary: This post reports that activation steering in Llama3.1-8B can bypass refusal even when the steering vector encodes a benign concept such as Portugal or brand identity, and that which vectors break refusal on which prompts is hard to predict. entry.title: The imposters among us: function vectors that ace every check and do the wrong task (in search of circularity)

author.name: star2vec

entry.summary: The authors show that shift-by-k-months function vectors extracted from low-diversity few-shot prompts on Llama-3.2-3B pass standard validation checks (behavioral gate, split-half stability, causal effect) while actually encoding a different task that ignores k. Lower input diversity paradoxically improves few-shot performance while favoring these impostor vectors, and no injection setting rescued them.

entry.title: Broadening access to Skala creates a faster path to predictive DFT

author.name: Sebastian Ehlert, Stefano Battaglia, Thijs Vogels, Jan Hermann, Jens Wehner, Giulia Luise, Klaas Giesbertz, Chin-Wei Huang, Aaron Kaplan, Kate Milton, Stephanie Marisa Lanius, Derk Kooi, P. Bernát Szabó, Gregor Simm, Rianne van den Berg, Paola Gori Giorgi

entry.summary: Microsoft Research describes Skala 1.1, an updated deep-learning exchange-correlation functional for density functional theory trained on about 2.5 times more data than the prior version, with improved accuracy on thermochemistry, reaction kinetics, and molecular structure. entry.title: Let's Scale Step by Step: Compute-Efficient Hyperparameter Transfer for Large-Scale Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Nayeon Kim, Hojin Lee, Yunju Bak, Jaesun Park, Boseop Kim

entry.summary: Presents a two-step, compute-efficient recipe for transferring optimal learning rates to very large Mixture-of-Experts models, first adapting maximal update parameterization to MoE with multi-head latent attention and the Muon optimizer, then extrapolating across widths and to trillion-token training horizons. This avoids prohibitively expensive hyperparameter sweeps at frontier scale.

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Scalable oversight anchors today's batch: a Google DeepMind result shows RL through a generator–critic debate game measurably reduces reward hacking of weaker LLM judges in RLAIF. entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF

author.name: Zachary Kenton, Lili Janzer, Rory Greig, Tian Huey Teh, Kirill Tyshchuk, Jonah Brown-Cohen, Harri Edwards, Senthooran Rajamanoharan, Noah Y. Siegel, Natasha Jaques, Rohin Shah

entry.summary: A Google DeepMind team shows that RL finetuning a policy through a debate game, where a generator and a critic argue and a weaker judge model decides, produces substantially less reward hacking than a standard RLAIF baseline on verifiable math tasks. Because final answers are checkable, the authors can directly measure how the policy exploits judge errors over training, in the crucial regime where the judge is weaker than the policy.

entry.title: Accurate Decoding of Natural Sentences from Non-Invasive Brain Recordings

author.name: Mingfang Zhang, Jarod L\'evy, Cedric Rommel, J\'er\'emy Rapin, Corentin Bel, Julie Bonnaire, Daniel Nieto, Pierre Bourdillon, Svetlana Pinet, St\'ephane d'Ascoli, Thomas Moreau, Jean-R\'emi King

entry.summary: Reports a non-invasive brain-to-text system that decodes typed natural sentences from magnetoencephalography using character, word, and sentence-level representations, trained on 22,000 sentences across nine subjects with ten hours each. Average word error rate reaches 39 percent, with the best participant decoded near half of sentences with at most one word error. This is the technical write-up of the Brain2Qwerty v2 line of work rather than a new product launch.

entry.title: Abra: Scaling Diffusion Image Training

author.name: Kyle Chickering, Wei-An Lin, Swayam Bhanded, Dan Saunders, Akshat Tripathi, Jiaming Song, Shyamal Buch, Xinchen Yan

entry.summary: Presents a systematic compute-optimal scaling law study for text-to-image diffusion using a controlled family of flow-matching transformers trained from about 10^19 to 10^22 FLOPs, three orders of magnitude of compute. The headline result is that diffusion models scale as predictably as language models but are far more data hungry, with compute optimality near 200 image tokens per parameter, roughly ten times the Chinchilla prescription for LLMs.

entry.title: Proactive Road Safety Intervention in Australia: Predicting Risky Driving Hotspots from Connected Vehicle Data

author.name: Adriana-Simona Mih\u{a}i\c{t}\u{a}, Clarence Cheung, Artur Grigorev, Tuo Mao, David Lillo-Trynes

entry.summary: SPADE is a self-play framework where one LLM alternates between designing complete executable training environments (Gym-style reset and step code with state, rewards and verification) and acting as the reasoning agent that learns in them, so the goal distribution expands as the learner improves. It aims to break the dependence of agent RL on hand-curated or frozen environment pools.

entry.title: Debate Training Reduces Reward Hacking in RLAIF

author.name: zac_kenton

entry.summary: A Google DeepMind Amplified Oversight team paper and blog post showing that when reinforcement learning is run against an LLM judge, the judge gets reward-hacked, and that inserting a debate opponent that argues against the trained policy substantially reduces this hacking. It applies debate to the fuzzy-task reward problem that arises even in coding, where passing tests is not the same as good code.

entry.title: ADEPT: Accelerating Dexterity via Pre-Training and Post-Training using Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jayjun Lee, Jessica Yin, Asif Rana, Nicholas Blauch, Sam Mady, Mohak Bhardwaj, Nima Fazeli, Nathan Ratliff, Karl Van Wyk, Ankur Handa

entry.summary: ADEPT is a large-scale reinforcement learning framework that pretrains a dexterous manipulation policy on a generic object-reposing task from raw visuo-tactile input, then reuses that behavior as a prior for long-horizon downstream tasks across high-DoF hands, with mechanisms to prevent fine-tuning from destroying the prior. The pretrained policy zero-shots the reposing stage of new tasks and transfers sim-to-real.

entry.title: How AI Prompts Can Teach Us About the Structure of Human Behavior

author.name: Matthew O. Jackson, Benjamin S. Manning, Yutong Xie, Walter Yuan, Qiaozhu Mei

entry.summary: Assigns LLMs numeric trait vectors such as altruism and risk aversion, then fits those vectors to reproduce human choices across 119,147 decisions by 78,657 subjects in ten classic economic games from 35-plus countries. The approach turns prompt dimensionality into an empirical estimate of how many latent traits are needed to describe human behavior.

entry.title: Coupled-cluster molecular properties across the main group that extrapolate beyond training size

author.name: Wenhao He, Xu Chen, Noah Song, Haowei Xu, Tim S. Hindges, Bohan Li, Zihan Lin, Yu Yao, Avetik R. Harutyunyan, Fang Liu, Yao Wang, Hao Tang, Ju Li

entry.summary: Trains an equivariant network to predict an effective one-electron Hamiltonian from a single cheap DFT calculation, then derives energies, gaps, dipoles, polarizabilities, charges, and bond orders at coupled-cluster accuracy across nine main-group elements. Reports extrapolation to molecules larger than those in training.

entry.title: GigaBrain-WBC-0.5: A Behavior World Model for Robust Whole-Body Control with Environment Interaction

author.name: Ziyang Cheng, Tianshu Tang, Jinxin Lan, Xinze Chen, Yuhan Gong, Zhichao Liu, Changzhong Wu, Yahao Mao, Zongyan Deng, Mingxuan Ma, Huasen Xi, Yilong Liu, Yutong Wu, Xiaofeng Wang, Yang Wang, Yun Ye, Guan Huang, Xiaojie Jin, Zheng Zhu, Jiwen Lu

entry.summary: Introduces a behavior world model for humanoid whole-body control that learns how terrain and object contact reshape dynamics, rather than training a purely reactive motion tracker on flat ground. The claim is that predicting environment interaction lets the low-level policy stay feasible when balance depends on the scene.

entry.title: Debiased Inference for AI-Generated Data without Gold-Standard Labels: Identification via Multiple Imperfect Measurements

author.name: Naoki Egami, Sooahn Shin

entry.summary: Proposes a statistical framework that debiases downstream analyses of AI-measured variables by combining several imperfect measurements instead of requiring expensive gold-standard human labels. Shows that treating high-accuracy AI labels as ground truth still produces biased estimates and invalid confidence intervals.

entry.title: The IOL-AI Challenge: An Open Challenge towards Advancing Linguistic Reasoning

author.name: Eduardo S\'anchez, Rita Berrada, Dan-Mircea Mirea, Sara Rajaee, Alexander Piperski, Ana Meta Dolinar, Boris Iomdin, Andrey Nikulin, Mariya Shmatova, Marzieh Fadaee, Julia Kreutzer

entry.summary: Reports on an open competition built on unseen International Linguistics Olympiad 2026 problems, where solutions were graded both automatically and, for the first time, by the official IOL jury using the same rubrics applied to human contestants. It drew 731 submissions from 46 teams under a strict one-GPU thirty-minute budget, and separately benchmarked 15 unconstrained frontier and open models, with Claude Opus 4.8 reaching a jury score equivalent to a gold medal.

entry.title: Children, but not language models, show accelerating returns in word learning

author.name: Michael C. Frank

entry.summary: Shows that children's vocabulary growth follows accelerating accumulation, learning more per additional unit of linguistic input over time, whereas language models, even those trained on child-directed speech, exhibit constant proportional returns consistent with scaling laws. The contrast identifies increasing input efficiency as a specific candidate mechanism behind the enormous sample-efficiency gap between children and LMs.

entry.title: Fool's Gold: Defensive Deception Against Safety-Removal Attacks on Open-Weight Models

author.name: Mark Russinovich

entry.summary: Proposes decoy hardening, a defense that accepts that abliteration will strip refusal behavior from open-weight models and instead trains the post-attack state to emit confident but factually falsified answers to hazardous operational requests. The defense is learned inside a differentiable simulation of the attack and tested on seven models from five families spanning 9B to 122B.

entry.title: Decomposition Attacks Across Unlinkable Identities: Limits of Stateful Defenses for LLM Services

author.name: Bowen Sun, Zhengyue Zhao, Xiaogeng Liu, Yinzhi Cao, Chaowei Xiao

entry.summary: Analyzes decomposition attacks in which an adversary splits a harmful task into individually benign requests issued under unlinkable identities, so no stateful monitor can group them. For a fixed non-retrying attack strategy the authors prove the achievable security-utility tradeoff is fully determined by a specific structural property, establishing limits on what stateful defenses can accomplish.

entry.title: Q-Learning With World Models

author.name: Perry Dong, Yueru Jia, Chelsea Finn, Dorsa Sadigh

entry.summary: This work asks how to use learned world models to improve off-policy Q-learning rather than to generate imagined rollouts for direct policy optimization, which suffers compounding bias at long horizons and high visual complexity. The stated target is sample-efficient RL fine-tuning of vision-language-action policies for real robots. It could sharpen how model-based components are integrated into value learning for robotics.

entry.title: PROBE: Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering with VLM Agents

author.name: Vineet Bhat, Siyi Chen, Alex Zook, Xuning Yang, Stan Birchfield, Valts Blukis, Jonathan Tremblay

entry.summary: Formalizes Manipulation-Grounded Visual Question Answering, where answering a question requires physically moving distractor objects to reveal occluded ones so the scene changes with each action. PROBE contributes a high-fidelity tabletop simulator plus a framework for benchmarking and finetuning VLM agents on this interactive perception setting.

entry.title: When AI art has no author: Study finds generated images often can’t be traced to training data

author.name: Rachel Gordon | MIT CSAIL

entry.summary: MIT CSAIL researchers identify what they call attribution decay: as generative image models are trained on more data, the counterfactual influence of any single training example, artist, or subject on a given output shrinks toward nothing, so removing that data often leaves outputs unchanged. They argue that if removal changes nothing, that data cannot be held responsible for the output, which undercuts data-attribution-based approaches to credit, licensing, and liability. The finding bears directly on active lawsuits and proposed regulation.

entry.title: Spectral Gaps of Hit-and-Run and Coordinate Hit-and-Run

author.name: Yunbum Kook, Santosh S. Vempala

entry.summary: Proves a new spectral gap bound for Hit-and-Run sampling on convex bodies expressed via the Poincare constant of the target rather than the outer radius, refining the classic Lovasz-Vempala mixing bound. Combined with recent KLS progress, this gives near-quadratic-in-dimension mixing for nearly isotropic bodies, and the paper also treats coordinate Hit-and-Run.

entry.title: There is No Theoretical Curse of Multilinguality For Embedding Space Structure

author.name: Niyati Bafna, Neha Verma, Vil\'em Zouhar, Philipp Koehn, David Yarowsky

entry.summary: Formalizes what perfect multilinguality would mean for an embedding space and proves that the minimum dimensionality needed grows only logarithmically in the number of languages, so the curse of multilinguality is not an inherent geometric constraint. The result reframes observed multilingual degradation as an artifact of training and capacity allocation rather than a representational impossibility.

entry.title: Hydra-0: Action Flow for Generalist World Modeling and Control

author.name: Hongyu Li, Bowen Wen, Xinghao Zhu, Yixuan Wang, Yilun Du, Yunzhu Li, George Konidaris, Stan Birchfield, Soha Pouya, Chenran Li, Yan Chang

entry.summary: Hydra-0 is a generalist world model conditioned on action flow, representing robot actions as pixel motion so a single visual interface transfers across embodiments, tasks, environments, and video generation backbones. The authors report large reductions in robot- and object-motion prediction error over an action-conditioned baseline, strong agreement between replayed and reference success rates on a robot benchmark, zero-shot composition, and an emergent inverse mode that infers compatible robot motion from video. This positions world models as both controllers and reliable policy evaluators.

entry.title: Advancing Open and Reproducible Relational Learning: RelArena-$\alpha$, TabPFN-Rel and RPI

author.name: Adrian Hayler, Klemens Fl\"oge, Alan Arazi, Rishabh Ranjan, Jure Leskovec, Felix Birkel, Brendan Roof, Anurag Garg, Kristina Collins, Lydia Sidhoum, Jonas K\"ubler, Siyuan Guo, Oscar Key, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Rylee Grace, David Salinas, Arthur Cahu, Simon Bing, Benjamin J\"ager, Tuana \c{C}elik, Mihir Manium, Vitor Monteiro, Jake Robertson, Jerry Chen, Eliott Kalfon, Tom\'as Pereda, Lilly Wehrhahn, Dominik Safaric, Tobias Schroeder, Georg Grab, Diana Kriuchkova, Clara Cornu, Philipp Singer, Nick Erickson, Vahid Balazadeh, Marie Salmon, Simone Alessi, K\"ur\c{s}at Kaya, Philipp Jund, L\'eo Grinsztajn, Yann LeCun, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Madelon Hulsebos, Lennart Purucker, Sauraj Gambhir, Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann

entry.summary: Prior Labs releases three open-source artifacts for relational (multi-table) learning: RelArena-alpha, a unified benchmarking framework; TabPFN-Rel, a relational extension of tabular in-context learning; and RPI, a supporting interface. The stated aim is to give the field a reproducible way to compare methods on relational tasks, with an alpha release aimed at researchers.

entry.title: Improving the matrix multiplication exponent with modern optimization and AlphaEvolve

author.name: Emilien Dupont, Marvin Eisenberger, Borislav Kozlovskii, Abbas Mehrabian, Francisco J. R. Ruiz, Abigail See, Renfei Zhou, Josh Alman, Virginia Vassilevska Williams, Matej Balog

entry.title: Proteus: Incremental Memory Activation for Long-Context Sequence Modeling

author.name: Reza Bayat, Ali Behrouz, Vahab Mirrokni, Aaron Courville

entry.summary: Proteus proposes incremental memory activation for long-context sequence models, progressively expanding the effective capacity of a compressed recurrent memory as the sequence grows rather than exposing a static state from the first token. The early bottleneck forces stronger compression of early history and reduces interference between stored context and incoming tokens.

entry.title: Physics of Agents: Statistical Mechanics Predicts Collective Behavior of AI Agents

author.name: Batu El, Jinhee Paeng, Fatih Dinc, Shiye Su, Mete Erdogan, Aneesh Pappu, Haotian Ye, Wanjia Zhao, Surya Ganguli, James Zou

entry.summary: The paper behind earlier this week's Reddit thread on agents spontaneously agreeing, Studying over ten thousand communities of language-model agents that exchange messages and revise opinions on both objective math questions and subjective political statements, the authors find the dynamics collapse into a small number of characteristic regimes and can be described with statistical mechanics style models. This makes collective behaviors such as herding and polarization predictable rather than anecdotal. It provides design guidance for multi-agent systems.

entry.title: Model Hypnosis: Strong control of AI via additive subliminal effects

author.name: Enric Boix-Adsera, Benedict Tessler

entry.summary: Reports model hypnosis, in which many individually negligible prompt cues such as paraphrases and typos can be additively combined to exert strong control over model behavior, and shows the effect across model families and scales including frontier reasoning models with transferable hypnotic prompts. The authors argue this creates a new class of safety and interpretability problems because control is exercised through inconspicuous surface choices.

entry.title: Emergent Misaligned Communication in Long-Horizon Multi-Agent LLM Commerce

author.name: Zeyuan Li (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Lukas Petersson (Andon Labs), Alessandro Acquisti (Massachusetts Institute of Technology), Michiel A. Bakker (Massachusetts Institute of Technology)

entry.summary: Analyzes 2,583 inter-agent emails from 20 simulated year-long runs of a competitive vending-machine business environment spanning 13 frontier LLMs, measuring speech-act misalignment such as false factual claims, manipulation, collusion, and threats. It moves beyond adversarial single-agent elicitation to measure how misaligned communication arises spontaneously in long-horizon, multi-principal commerce.

author.name: Adam Karvonen, Euan Ong, Subhash Kantamneni, Samuel Marks

entry.summary: This paper evaluates explanations of model behavior by counterfactual simulatability, whether an explanation predicts what the model does on related edited inputs, and introduces CHIVE, an agentic pipeline that finds unexpected behaviors in real usage and probes them with counterfactual prompt edits. It produces thousands of explanations with supporting counterfactual evidence for naturally occurring behaviors.

entry.title: ClawGym II: Exploring Black-Box RL on Agent Harness

author.name: Huatong Song, Fei Bai, Ming Yang, Renyuan Li, Jia Deng, Jujie He, Zhange Zhang, Daixuan Cheng, Yan Xing, Qi Yun, Xuxing Chen, Danyang Li, Feng Chang, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Jian Yang, Bryan Dai, Wayne Xin Zhao, Mingjie Tang, Ji-Rong Wen

entry.summary: ClawGym II builds a black-box reinforcement learning framework for training agents through complex, opaque agent harnesses, using sandboxed concurrent rollouts and a serving proxy at the model boundary to capture trajectories without instrumenting harness internals. This decouples policy optimization from harness execution so long-horizon agentic RL can scale.

entry.title: Research Summary: August 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's strongest work clusters around automating AI research itself, the fragility of interpretability and benchmark evidence, and pretraining data economics.

  • AI Research Preference Models score candidate experiments before execution, attacking the evaluation-compute bottleneck that dominates autonomous research agents
  • Toby Ord's formal treatment of intelligence explosion dynamics shows true singular growth requires stricter feedback conditions than governance discourse assumes

Interpretability and measurement validity form the dominant theme, with two papers in direct tension. An MIT circuit study across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains reports spontaneous brain-like functional modularity; a pre-registered grid of 15,840 specifications on GPT-2 small IOI circuits shows such findings often do not survive defensible analytic variation. On evaluation: post-training on SWE-bench trajectories transfers poorly to a purpose-built Django suite, and Behavioral Lift demonstrates that amplified reasoning behaviors in thinking models are weakly predictive of correctness.

  • A unified path-space policy-gradient view derives reverse-trajectory and forward-matching diffusion RL objectives from one framework, consolidating a fragmented area
  • A Year in LLM Serving releases rare long-horizon production traces with actionable caching and load-balancing implications
  • Also notable: Jais 2 Arabic-centric open model family (MBZUAI/Cerebras/Inception), thermodynamically consistent universal interatomic potentials, and a full ImageNet-1k validation re-annotation

entry.title: Modular Cognitive Architecture Emerges in Large Language Models

author.name: Pengrui Han, Jacob Andreas, Evelina Fedorenko, Andrea Gregor de Varda

entry.summary: Uses circuit analysis across 46 tasks in four cognitive domains to test whether language models spontaneously develop brain-like functional specialization, and reports that distinct circuits handle language, formal reasoning, social reasoning, and physical reasoning. entry.title: AI Research Preference Models

author.name: Thomas Simon Foster, Bassel Al Omari, Tingchen Fu, Thomas Mann, Carl Domond, Lucia Cipolina-Kun, Bhavul Gauri, Muna Aghamelu, Alexander D. Goldie, Eryk Helenowski, Jean-Christophe Gagnon-Audet, Alberto Pepe, Saba Nazir, Daniel Izcovich, Noam Levi, Rishi Hazra, Karen Hambardzumyan, Nicolas Baldwin, Xian Li, Martin Josifoski, Paris Giampouras, Masoud Jalili Sabet, Anya Sims, Hela Momand, Tatiana Shavrina, Despoina Magka, Jason Weston, Yulin Wang, Anirudh Goyal, Jo\~ao Henriques, Yoram Bachrach, Emily McMilin, Jakob Nicolaus Foerster

The authors build research preference models from frozen pretrained language models that predict which candidate solutions are worth actually running, without task-specific training.

author.name: Kai Chen, Jifeng Ding, Ning Ding, Jiaye Ge, Lixin Gu, Yicheng Gu, Qipeng Guo, Ermo Hua, Haian Huang, Haozheng Hou, Jie Hou, Xiangyu Hong, Che Jiang, Minxi Jin, Cheng Liang, Dahua Lin, Dawei Liu, Kuikun Liu, Chengqi Lv, Haijun Lv, Han Lv, Ningsheng Ma, Biqing Qi, Jianmin Qian, Shiya Su, Youbang Sun, Huanze Tang, Zhongbo Tian, Hanjing Wang, Rui Wang, Ting Wang, Yi Wang, Baiting Wu, Jun Xu, Bowen Yang, Hui Wang, Weida Wang, Haochen Ye, Jiashuo Yu, Shan Yu, Xiaoyi Yu, Qirui Zeng, Qi Zhang, Ming Zhang, Wenwei Zhang, Bowen Zhou, Xinyu Zhou

A 7B model trained from scratch reportedly matches a transformer baseline using about 63 percent of the training data, and a continually pretrained version builds on the existing Qwen3.5-35B model. If it holds up, decoupling knowledge from reasoning is a substantive departure from the standard transformer block.

entry.title: The Dynamics of Intelligence Explosions

author.name: Toby Ord

entry.summary: Toby Ord analyzes the mathematics of AI-accelerated AI research feedback loops, showing that true singular growth toward a vertical asymptote is harder to obtain than recent economics-style models suggest, and highlighting a neglected regime of super-exponential but non-singular growth. He argues the loop generation time is a pivotal and usually ignored parameter. The paper sharpens quantitative discussion of takeoff speeds that underpins much AI policy debate.

entry.title: Scaling Domain Data Repetition in LLM Pretraining

author.name: Jingwei Li, Xinran Gu, Rui Dai, Xintong Hao, Chengyin Xu, Yan Wu, Shuran Zheng, Jingzhao Zhang

entry.summary: Studies how many times scarce high-quality domain data should be repeated in LLM pretraining when the token budget grows with model size, finding that at fixed tokens-per-parameter the optimal repetition count mildly increases with model scale. This directly addresses the dilution of specialist data as general web corpora dominate larger training mixtures. The results provide actionable scaling guidance for pretraining data mixture design.

entry.title: Don't Claim Benchmark-Oriented Optimization Improves General Coding Capability -- Diverse Evaluation Is Required

author.name: Egor Shibaev, Vera Kudrevskaia, Timur Galimzyanov, Mikhail Evtikhiev, Ana Terna, Rastislav Rabatin, Timur Kudashev, Timofey Bryksin, Arina Puchkova, Patrik Bartak, Egor Bogomolov, Sergey Titov

entry.summary: Using a purpose-built Django case-study suite, the authors show that post-training on SWE-bench trajectories yields little transfer to other coding tasks and that benchmark rankings frequently fail to generalize, undermining the common practice of citing a handful of coding scores as evidence of general coding ability. They argue for diverse evaluation before claiming broad capability. The results are a direct challenge to how model cards and post-training papers report coding progress.

entry.title: Designing Reinforcement Learning for Diffusion Models: A Unified Path-Space View

author.name: Yixian Xu, Yuanrui Zhang, Shengjie Luo, Liwei Wang, Di He

entry.summary: Shows that reverse-trajectory and forward-matching reinforcement learning objectives for diffusion models both fall out of a single path-space policy-gradient principle derived via importance sampling between sampling SDEs. This unification explains Flow-GRPO-style updates as special cases and suggests principled design choices for new diffusion RL algorithms.
